newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper stocks tipped to rise, aluminium down.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stocks tipped to rise, aluminium down.

text.p: Copper stocks on the London Metal Exchange (LME) appear set to rise by 2,000 to 5,000 tonnes while aluminium should persist in its recent slide by falling another 2,000-4,000 tonnes, base metal traders said on Friday.

"We feel it (copper) should be up 3,000-5,000 tonnes, but feel it will probably be closer to 5,000 tonnes," the general manager of a European metal trading firm said. The LME stocks report will be released later on Friday.
A senior dealer for a Japanese trading house expected, however, copper istocks would rise by only 2,000-3,000 tonnes.
"An increase in copper may be more modest," he said.
Aluminium inventories will probably slip by 2,000-4,000 tonnes, continuing the recent downward trend.
"Ally (aluminium) should be down about 2,000 to 4,000 tonnes," one dealer said. In the last LME report on Tuesday, aluminium stocks fell by 3,925 tonnes.
The volume of copper in the LME warehouse in Singapore may increase slightly as people drift slowly back to the market after the recent holiday period, dealers said.
Any significant rise in Singapore metal stocks is not expected until after most of the Far East trade returns to work on Monday as many delaers took an extended Chinese Lunar New Year holiday.
On Tuesday, the quantity of copper in the LME's Singapore warehouse reached 53,175 tonnes, up 500 tonnes from the previous Friday's report.
Dealers said a surge in zinc prices on the LME, where the metal hit a two-year peak on Thursday of US$1,228 a tonne, prompted Chinese sellers to park some of the metal in warehouses in Singapore.

Up to 10,000 tonnes of zinc may remain off-warrant here, dealers said. The amount of zinc in the LME's Singapore warehouse reached 5,200 tonnes on Tuesday, unchanged from the previous Friday's report.
Three month copper prices were quoted by regional dealers at 0200 GMT at around $2,270/75 a tonne, almost unchanged from late trade in London on Thursday at $2,270/73 a tonne.
Aluminium was seen a tad higher here at about $1,576/80 a tonne against the close in London on Thursday of $1,576 a tonne.
